questions.q: What is the primary condition for two shapes to be called congruent?
questions.a: Two shapes are congruent if they have the same shape and the same size. A wrong answer suggests the student confuses congruence with similarity (same shape but different size).

questions.q: If you have two triangles where all three sides are equal, but you haven't measured the angles, can you say they are congruent? Why?
questions.a: Yes, because the SSS (Side-Side-Side) rule states that if three sides of one triangle are equal to the three sides of another, the triangles are congruent. A wrong answer suggests the student is not yet familiar with the congruence shortcuts for triangles.

questions.q: If two squares have a side length of 5 cm each, are they congruent? Explain the steps to verify.
questions.a: Yes. Step 1: Measure all sides (all 5 cm). Step 2: Measure all angles (all 90 degrees). Step 3: Attempt to superimpose one over the other. Step 4: Confirm they match exactly. A wrong answer shows confusion between "equal area" and "congruence."

questions.q: Compare a small photograph and a large poster of the same person. Are they congruent? Analyze the relationship between their shape and size.
questions.a: They are not congruent because their sizes are different. While they have the same "shape" (similarity), congruence requires the dimensions to be identical, which they are not in this case.

questions.q: Critique this statement: "If two triangles have the same angles, they must be congruent." Is this always true?
questions.a: This is false. Two triangles can have the same angles but different side lengths (like a small and large equilateral triangle), meaning they are not congruent. A wrong answer shows the student assumes angles alone define size.

questions.q: Draw two different pairs of shapes: one pair that is congruent and one pair that is not congruent, using everyday objects like coins or notebooks.
questions.a: The student should draw or describe objects like two identical 10-rupee notes (congruent) versus a 10-rupee note and a 20-rupee note (not congruent). A poor answer fails to distinguish between objects of different sizes.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Two ______ shapes are congruent if they have the exact same shape and size, meaning one can be placed perfectly over the other so that all edges and corners match.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever noticed that two ______ pages from your notebook can be placed perfectly on top of each other?
What is Two geometric shapes? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Two geometric shapes are congruent if they have the exact same shape and size, meaning one can be placed perfectly over the other so that all edges and corners match.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: If you take two identical bangles or two ______-rupee coins, you will notice that they have the same size and shape—they are "congruent." To start, visualize picking up one shape and laying it down on the other; if it covers the shape underneath without any part sticking out or any gaps, they are congruent.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Two geometric shapes?
questions.a: Students often confuse "congruent" with "similar." They think if shapes look alike (like two triangles of different sizes), they are congruent.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to visually identify congruent shapes and explain that they "fit" perfectly when superimposed, and identify corresponding parts in congruent triangles.
